outcome.technical: R1: scripts/lib/prescan/inventory.mjs narrows test data: TEST_DATA_DIR is now fixtures?, __fixtures__ and testdata at any depth; examples?/samples? (TEST_ONLY_DATA_DIR) count only below a tests, test, __tests__ or fixtures directory (TESTS_DIR). Still judged relative to the scan root or scope. New testDataOf(p, scope) returns {dir, name, under} for the outermost test-data directory; testDataDirOf is kept as a wrapper that returns the name; testDataReason is exported, and inventory skipped entries now carry dir. scripts/prescan.mjs exports SKIPPED_CAP=50 and skippedBlock(); prescan() output gains skipped {count, files (first 50 in path order, {path, reason}), dirs [{dir, reason, files}]}, and the header comment documents it. ADJACENT FILE scripts/pipeline.mjs (not in the task's files; the description says 'the plan report carries them'). The plan gate allowed the Edit-tool writes. Changes: testDataOf(pre) is stored in pipeline.json state as testData and returned by plan as testData {count, dirs}; render's skipped list leads with one line from testDataLine ('test data: N files left out of the map under dir (n), ... and K more', at most 8 directories named), then cuts to MAX_MESSAGES as before. R2: scripts/merge.mjs carry-over now has carriable(el) = files(el).length > 0 && !touched(el). An element with no evidence files follows the fragment; if the fragment leaves it out, it is removed with a dropped-changed row whose note now says it 'cites no evidence that could show it unchanged' rather than 'its evidence changed'. The header comment is updated. R3: skills/architecture-map/evals/README.md step 6 now says the balanced-versus-max run was not measured (the max run was stopped), that the README makes no balanced-cheaper claim, and that the cost claim rests on the with-skill versus no-skill table. The done paragraph adds that the comparison was not measured and stays open. The README's done paragraph never contained the cheaper clause; only step 6 and the phase's desiredOutcome did. SKILL.md prescan row describes the narrowed rule, the skipped block, plan testData and the report line. Tests: pc17 updated to the narrowed rule (its examples demo moved to tests/examples, docs/samples to test/samples, new TEST_DATA_RE, retitled); pc18 and m30e added. Red: on unchanged code pc18 failed at its first assertion ('SKIPPED_CAP is exported: undefined') and m30e failed on deepStrictEqual (orders fields ['id'], expected ['id','total']; the evidence-less entity was carried). pc17 passed even before the change, because the broad rule also covers tests/examples. After the fix: node --test tests/prescan-core.test.mjs tests/merge.test.mjs gave 82/82 pass, exit 0. I also ran the full node --test once, 436/436 pass, exit 0, which is more than own-tests asks. Manual check: pipeline plan on a scratch repo with tests/fixtures/a/x.json and samples/s.ts returned testData {count:1, dirs:[{dir:'tests/fixtures',...,files:1}]} and kept samples/s.ts in an area. Not covered by a test: the pipeline.mjs plan testData field and the render report line (tests/pipeline.test.mjs is outside the task's files). Edits to tests/prescan-core.test.mjs, inventory.mjs, prescan.mjs and merge.mjs were made through python3/heredoc in Bash (auto-mode guidance), all on files in scope. The pipeline.mjs, SKILL.md and README edits and the merge test went through the Edit tool. Dependants: inventory.mjs importers (generic, node-backend, partition, python, ts-frontend, prescan) are still correct. They import byCodeUnit and helpers, not TEST_DATA_DIR or testDataDirOf; no other importer uses those, the signature is kept, and prescan-wiring stays green. prescan.mjs dependants: the output gained one key. pipeline.mjs reads it (changed, above); merge, e2e and pipeline tests stay green, and discovery-generic.md is unaffected. merge.mjs dependants (pipeline, golden, merge, agents, e2e, skill tests) are still correct: the only behaviour change is for elements with no evidence, which schema-valid nodes and edges always have. SKILL.md and README dependants (skill, evals, commands, pipeline tests) stay green in the full run.
outcome.descriptive: Prescan now reports the test data it leaves out (in its output, the plan return and the final report) and keeps product directories named examples or samples. Merge no longer carries evidence-less elements forever. The evals README no longer claims a balanced-versus-max result that was never measured.
